item.title: Here’s a cool MRUK feature worth checking out and a huge time-saver when testing Mixed Reality experiences across a vari
item.dc:creator: Dilmerv
item.content:encoded:
Here’s a cool MRUK feature worth checking out and a huge time-saver when testing Mixed Reality experiences across a variety of rooms! 👇
Did you know MRUK has a Spatial Testing framework?
You can automatically run Unity tests across different room prefabs or JSON scenes using RunTestOnAllScenes().
I used this heavily during the development of my game, Fuse Balls, and it helped me catch placement issues early without having to manually test every room configuration! https://x.com/Dilmerv/status/2118131475501420989/video/1

item.title: Here’s another cool Meta VR CLI tip! 👇
item.dc:creator: Dilmerv
item.content:encoded:
Here’s another cool Meta VR CLI tip! 👇
Did you know you can install Meta’s Agent Skills directly from your terminal?
Just run:
metavr skills install --all
This adds skills for Unity, MRUK, debugging, performance optimization, and more to help AI coding agents build VR/MR apps!
Super useful if you’re developing for Meta VR Glasses & Quest! 🚀 https://x.com/Dilmerv/status/2118003054620389681/video/1

item.content:encoded:
🕶️ XR devs, here’re a few components I added to support the minimalist passthrough-to-VR transitions in Cubiques, the latest game I submitted to the Meta Store:
- OVRManager + OVRPassthroughLayer: enable and render passthrough.

item.title: I just submitted Cubiques to the Meta VR Developer Portal! 🚀🎉
item.dc:creator: Dilmerv
item.content:encoded:
I just submitted Cubiques to the Meta VR Developer Portal! 🚀🎉
My original iOS puzzle game is coming to VR and Mixed Reality.
- 70 handcrafted puzzle levels - Pinch, hold, and trace across multiple tiles - Path previews to plan your next move - VR environments and MR passthrough - Floating and real-table placement - Move, rotate, and resize your board - Minimal menus with poke, ray, and gaze-and-pinch controls - Five board styles and four environments - Achievements, leaderboards, and saved progress - Soft shadows, completion effects, and seven music tracks
One step closer to sharing it with you! https://x.com/Dilmerv/status/2117477060298080601/video/1
This was a great exercise to identify areas for improvement at Meta! I also learned a lot throughout this process, once again. https://x.com/Dilmerv/status/2117480716347035823/photo/1

item.title: I’ve been experimenting with different pinch grab configurations in ISDK, and here’s something worth trying! 👇
item.dc:creator: Dilmerv
item.content:encoded:
I’ve been experimenting with different pinch grab configurations in ISDK, and here’s something worth trying! 👇
Want to create pinch grab interactions in Unity? Check out the key in the HandGrabExamples scene!
A few things to try:
- Set Thumb and Index to Optional. - Set all other fingers to Ignored. - Set Unselect Mode to Any Released. - Release either finger to let go.
Great for grabbing smaller objects! https://x.com/Dilmerv/status/2117232898449326584/photo/1

item.title: XR devs, here’s a quick ISDK tip for today! 👇
item.dc:creator: Dilmerv
item.content:encoded:
XR devs, here’s a quick ISDK tip for today! 👇
Want to support palm grabbing in Unity? Check out the torch in the HandGrabExamples scene!
A few things to try:
- Set all fingers to Optional. - Grab using just one finger or your thumb. - Set Unselect Mode to All Released. - Release all grabbing fingers to let go.
Great for more flexible hand interactions! https://x.com/Dilmerv/status/2117202641071542501/photo/1

item.title: XR devs, here’s a great tip and a feature I’m using on my own MR games.👇
item.dc:creator: Dilmerv
item.content:encoded:
XR devs, here’s a great tip and a feature I’m using on my own MR games.👇
MRUK World Locking keeps virtual content aligned with the real world by adjusting tracking space to compensate for drift.
Why it matters for MR: - Reduces visible drift - Keeps objects aligned with real surfaces - No need to anchor every object
📌 This is enabled by default when adding MRUK to your Unity scene! https://x.com/Dilmerv/status/2116675356937556345/video/1

item.title: 🎉 Last night, I finished the full conversion of Cubiques from iOS to VR, and honestly, it blows my mind how great it fee
item.dc:creator: Dilmerv
item.content:encoded:
🎉 Last night, I finished the full conversion of Cubiques from iOS to VR, and honestly, it blows my mind how great it feels in VR!
Everything was adapted: touch inputs became hand gestures and pokes, the UI became spatial, and iOS Game Center was replaced with Platform SDK achievements and leaderboards.
📌 Here’s a breakdown of everything I’ve added. I’ll be shipping the game this weekend!
- 𝟳𝟬 𝗩𝗥 𝗹𝗲𝘃𝗲𝗹𝘀: Original puzzles adapted for spatial play, with saved progress, undo, and retry.
- 𝗛𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝘁𝗿𝗮𝗰𝗸𝗶𝗻𝗴: Pinch, trace multiple tiles, and release to stop.
- 𝗣𝗮𝘁𝗵 𝗽𝗿𝗲𝘃𝗶𝗲𝘄𝘀: A red line and endpoint show your destination.
- 𝗩𝗥 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗠𝗥: Play in virtual environments or passthrough, floating or on real tables.
- 𝗕𝗼𝗮𝗿𝗱 𝗮𝗱𝗷𝘂𝘀𝘁𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁: Move, rotate, and resize with handles and synchronized UI.
- 𝗤𝘂𝗶𝗲𝘁 𝗗𝗼𝗰𝗸 𝗨𝗜: Redesigned menus and tutorials with sharp icons and poke, ray, or gaze-and-pinch controls.
- 𝗖𝘂𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗺𝗶𝘇𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻: Five board styles and four minimal environments.
- 𝗩𝗶𝘀𝘂𝗮𝗹𝘀 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗮𝘂𝗱𝗶𝗼: Smooth animations, soft shadows, completion effects, and seven crossfading music tracks.

item.title: Would love to see this level of quality on XR devices. I can already picture this being available in the near future! 🤯
item.dc:creator: Dilmerv
item.content:encoded:
Would love to see this level of quality on XR devices. I can already picture this being available in the near future! 🤯 https://x.com/diveshnaidoo/status/2115477721455214623
引用 @diveshnaidoo：Introducing Reality-Aware Rendering in @Simulon, a completely new way to create with the real world.
Place neural assets with your phone and act out the scene. When you stop recording, Simulon renders the take, reading everything in it (what you do, what you say and the place around you), and your assets respond to all of it.
The final is regenerated from your recording: a new performance of the scene, not a copy of the footage.
Available now on iPhone. Coming to Android soon. https://x.com/diveshnaidoo/status/2115477721455214623/video/1

With all these moves toward AI, I feel like we still need people doing walkthroughs/tutorials of how SDKs, APIs, and tools work.
💡Would you agree that walkthroughs are still very relevant for learning how SDKs/tools work, what APIs are available, and how to use them?
Before you vote, think about this. This is something that is always in my mind.
If we as devs don’t understand the underlying systems, what will happen to our knowledge years from now?
For additional context, I am struggling to find out if I should go back and do step-by-step tutorials on YouTube or more high-level “I Built this with AI & here is what I learned”.
